# Kalle Westerling

> Kalle Westerling is a Staff Developer Relations Engineer at Chainguard, where he creates courses, hands-on labs, workshops and live demos that help developers adopt secure container images and open-source libraries. He also builds open-source tools for developer educators, from testing code examples in published courses to pacing live sessions. Before Chainguard he was a research software engineer and research application manager at the Alan Turing Institute, and before that he led national coding and research training programs at CUNY, where he earned a PhD in digital humanities. He still approaches technical education as a teacher first.

I teach developers how to ship secure software, and I build the tools that make that teaching hold up. At Chainguard I create courses, hands-on labs, workshops and live demos on container images, open-source libraries and software supply chain security.

Role: Staff Developer Relations Engineer at Chainguard (https://www.chainguard.dev)
Topics: Supply chain security, Containers, AI and agents, CTFs and games, Open source, Research and humanities
Contact: kallewesterling@gmail.com. For talks, workshops, podcasts and anything about developer education or software supply chain security.

## Courses

- [Chainguard Courses](https://courses.chainguard.dev): Where most of my work happens. Free, self-paced courses, learning paths and certifications for developers, security teams and platform engineers who want to secure their software supply chain with Chainguard Containers, Libraries and VMs.

## Tools I build

- [cvediff](https://github.com/kallewesterling/cvediff): Compares the known CVEs in two container images side by side in the terminal. Answers one question fast: what changes if we swap this base image for a hardened one?
- [errata](https://github.com/kallewesterling/errata): Finds broken code examples inside published course content, and keeps a dated record of the ones you can't fix yet. Courses stay live; the code in them shouldn't rot.
- [CodexMachina](https://westerling.nu/): Extracts, runs and lints the code blocks in Markdown and HTML documentation, with output verification, so every example in the docs is one you can trust.
- [session-pacer](https://westerling.nu/session-pacer/): A presenter view for timed talks, workshops and demos. Shows the notes for the current section, tells you when you're behind, and suggests what to cut.
- [syncjar](https://westerling.nu/syncjar/): Edit, preview and sync Skilljar course content locally, so course authors get a real git workflow instead of a web form.
- [credjar](https://westerling.nu/credjar/): Inspect, issue and revoke Credly badges from the command line, for certification programs that outgrow spreadsheets.

## Capture the flag and games

- Operation Lockdown (Capture the flag): A team capture-the-flag in two halves. First you break in: exploit the weaknesses in a container image and its software supply chain. Then you fix them the secure way. Run for customers, partners and communities. Played in Paris · Dresden · Stockholm.
- Faithful by Default (Capture the flag): A themed edition of Operation Lockdown, run together with Somerford. Same attack-then-fix format, new theme. Played in London.
- Cards Against Vulnerabilities (Card game): A security card game I designed for conference floors. First played at the RSA Conference AppSec Village, then scaled to about 200 players at DEF CON 34. Played in San Francisco · Las Vegas.
